name: 74HC4067 16-Channel Analog Multiplexer
summary: Turns one ADC pin into sixteen. An analog switch, not a buffer, so it passes signals both ways and brings its own resistance along.
notes: S2 and S3 are not in the order you expect. Going down the package it reads S0 (10), S1 (11), GND (12), S3 (13), S2 (14). Wire by name, not by walking the pins, or channel 4 and channel 8 will swap on you.
S0 is the least significant select bit and S3 the most, so the channel number is just the four bits read as a binary number.
E (pin 15) is active low. High turns every switch off, which is useful for sharing one ADC between several of these. Tie it to ground if you are not using it; it must not float.
This is a switch, not an amplifier. The signal has to stay between GND and VCC, so it cannot pass a waveform that swings negative without biasing it first.

On resistance is about 80 ohms at 6 V and 90 at 4.5 V, up to 180 at worst case, and it changes with the signal level. Into a high-impedance ADC that does not matter; driving anything that draws current, it is a divider you did not design.
After switching channels, give the ADC time. The sample capacitor has to charge through that on resistance, and reading immediately gives you a blend of the last channel and this one.
It is bidirectional, so the same part is a 1-to-16 demultiplexer with the signal going the other way. The CD4051 is the 8-channel version of the same idea.

circuit.title: Minimum circuit as a 16-input expander

parts.why: Supply decoupling at the pin. Switching all sixteen channels pulls charge out of the rail in steps.
E is active low, so grounding it keeps the selected switch on. Floating leaves the whole chip in an undefined state.
The common pin is the one analog input all sixteen channels share. S0 to S3 pick which one reaches it.

circuit.note: S0 to S3 go to four ordinary GPIOs. Nothing else is needed: the channels connect straight to whatever you are measuring, as long as it sits between GND and VCC.

pins.name: COM
pins.note: The shared end. To your ADC pin when multiplexing in, from your source when demultiplexing out.

pins.name: S0
pins.note: Least significant bit of the channel number.

pins.name: S3
pins.note: Most significant bit, and it comes before S2 in the package. This is the pin people miswire.

pins.name: E
pins.note: Low enables. High disconnects all sixteen channels.

pins.name: VCC
pins.note: Also the upper limit on any signal passing through the switches.
